summary: Kaiserslautern manages city-centre parking with a two-zone on-street regime under the fee ordinance in force from 1 May 2023: a core zone at 1.00 euro per 30 minutes with a 3-hour limit and an outer zone at 1.00 euro per hour or 5.00 euro per day, charged Monday to Saturday 8:00-19:00 except public holidays. An earlier ordinance of June 2019 charged 0.50 euro per 25 minutes in the core zone. Resident permits cost 100 euro for six months, 200 euro for a year and 400 euro for two years under an ordinance in force since 1 February 2024 (a Rheinpfalz teaser says the annual fee in the inner city rose from 30 euro), and 14 new paid 30-minute spaces in Richard-Wagner-Straße and Eisenbahnstraße were introduced on 15 July 2026 (reported on 27 July 2026). The garages are run by private operators: Contipark (City 400 spaces, Lutrinastraße 220, Hauptbahnhof P2 359), Q-Park (Pfalztheater 296, Stiftsplatz 180) and Park Service Hüfner (Altstadt Rittersberg 372, Pfaff Areal 361); APCOA lists the 490-space K in Lautern garage while the city's page still points to Q-Park, so its operator is unclear. The city runs a parking guidance system with 34 dynamic signs for four areas (Nord 990, West 1,020, Ost 530 and Hauptbahnhof 360 connected spaces) and publishes live free-space counts. A 2016 survey in the Mobilitätsplan Klima+ 2030 (adopted by the council on 5 February 2018) found garages often lightly used (partly below 20 percent) and street parking overloaded, and the report pointed to the price structure as one reason; those findings are about ten years old and the report does not show which measures followed. Opening hours differ by garage: Contipark's City and Lutrinastraße garages list no Sunday opening, while Q-Park and Hüfner list 24-hour access. The Rheinpfalz reported that the 360-space station garage at Hauptbahnhof was closed from 19 May 2025 for almost three months (full articles paywalled; reason and reopening not confirmed here). On match days the municipal utility SWK runs free P+R shuttles from KL-Ost and the university, and the city page says there is no public parking in the Betzenberg residential area; that page also contains some outdated text.

items.text: The city's parking fee ordinance in force from 1 May 2023 splits paid on-street parking into a core zone (resident zones 1-3: 1.00 euro per 30 minutes, 3-hour maximum stay unless signed otherwise) and an outer zone (zones 4-12: 1.00 euro per hour, 5.00 euro day ticket). Charges apply Monday to Saturday 8:00-19:00 except public holidays; the Messeplatz has a special tariff of 0.50 euro per 3 hours, 1.00 euro per day or 4.00 euro per week (Mon-Sat).
items.source_title: Parkgebührenordnung der Stadt Kaiserslautern (in Kraft ab 01.05.2023)

items.text: An earlier fee ordinance, in force from 1 June 2019, charged 0.50 euro per 25 minutes in the core zone (maximum stay 2 hours 55 minutes) and 0.50 euro per 50 minutes or 3.00 euro per day in the outer zone, Monday to Saturday 8:00-19:00. In hourly terms that is about 1.20 euro per hour in the core zone, against 2.00 euro per hour (1.00 euro per 30 minutes) under the ordinance of 1 May 2023, and a 3.00 euro against a 5.00 euro outer-zone day ticket. The 2023 ordinance says it replaced an ordinance of 1 May 2022, which was not read, so the 2019-to-2023 changes may have happened in steps.

Resident parking permits in Kaiserslautern's resident parking areas cost 100 euro for six months, 200 euro for one year and 400 euro for two years under a fee ordinance that took effect on 1 February 2024 (15 euro for changes or replacements). A Rheinpfalz teaser of 20 February 2024 (paywalled) says the annual fee in the inner city rose from 30 to 200 euro and that about 8,000 permits were in circulation.

The city's parking-management page (read on 21 October 2026) says demand for parking in the inner city exceeds supply, which is why paid parking with two tariff zones exists; stated aims are efficient use of spaces for customers, visitors and residents, higher turnover through the 3-hour limit in the core zone, and a stronger incentive to use bus, rail, bicycle and walking. It also lists a Messeplatz special permit at 150 euro per year and says that on car parks of the Gartenschau GmbH the fee is 3.00 euro, Monday to Sunday 8:00-22:00 (the page does not state the unit).

Since 15 July 2026 the city has 14 new paid 30-minute short-stay spaces (1 euro per 30 minutes) in Richard-Wagner-Straße and Eisenbahnstraße, following a 2023 council decision; during charging hours (Mon-Sat 8-19) holders of resident permits may no longer use them. The new machines are the city's first card-only pay machines (licence plate entered at the machine).
items.source_title: Kaiserslautern: 14 neue Kurzzeitparkplätze in der Innenstadt eingerichtet (Wochenblatt Reporter, 27 July 2026)

items.text: A city parking-space statute (Stellplatzsatzung), in force since 1 March 2022, governs how many car and bicycle spaces new buildings must provide. Where the spaces cannot be built, the developer can pay an in-lieu amount set by a separate statute (undated on the page) of 12,700 euro (zone I), 8,400 euro (zone II) or 5,700 euro (zone III) per space; the city uses the money for parking facilities, public transport or cycling investment, or measures that reduce parking demand. Page undated, read on 21 October 2026.

The city runs a parking guidance system with 34 dynamic signs leading to the connected car parks, grouped into four colour-coded areas: Centrum Nord (990 connected spaces), Centrum West (1,020), Centrum Ost (530) and Hauptbahnhof (360). Live free-space counts are published on the city website (page read on 21 October 2026); the city's car-park pages call Meuthstraße I and II surface lots and Pfalztheater, Stiftsplatz and Sparkasse underground garages.
items.source_title: Parkleitsystem und aktuelle Parkplatzbelegung - Stadt Kaiserslautern

items.text: Contipark's own pages (read 21 October 2026) list Parkhaus City Löwenstraße with 400 spaces (open Mon-Sat 07:00-20:30, no Sunday opening listed, no lift) and Parkhaus Lutrinastraße with 220 spaces (Mon-Fri 07:00-20:00, Sat 09:00-18:00). Both charge 1.50 euro for each of the first two half-hours, 2.50 euro per further hour and a 16.00 euro daily maximum (Pcard: 1.00 euro first hour, 1.50 euro per further hour, 8.00 euro maximum).

The Hauptbahnhof P2 Park+Ride garage (Zollamtstraße 5, DB BahnPark operated via Contipark) has 359 spaces and is open 24 hours; tariff 2.00 euro per hour, 12.00 euro per day (8.50 euro with Pcard), monthly 59.00 euro with a public-transport season ticket or 87.00 euro without. Page read on 21 October 2026.
items.source_title: Parkhaus Hauptbahnhof P2 Park+Ride in Kaiserslautern (Contipark)

items.text: According to the visible teasers of two Rheinpfalz articles (the full texts are paywalled), the Contipark-operated DB BahnPark garage at Hauptbahnhof, a garage with 360 spaces, was fully closed from Monday 19 May 2025 for almost three months, which mainly affects commuters. A Rheinpfalz piece of 22 May 2025 asks whether the feared chaos in the neighbouring quarter has happened and quotes one resident saying everything is as usual. The reason for the closure and the reopening date are not confirmed here.
items.source_title: Gesperrtes DB-Parkhaus: So ist die Lage (Rheinpfalz, 22 May 2025)

items.text: Park Service Hüfner lists two Kaiserslautern garages (page read 21 October 2026): Altstadtparkhaus Rittersberg, Salzstraße 7, with 372 spaces (1.00 euro per half hour, 2.00 euro per hour from the 4th hour, 16.00 euro daily maximum, licence-plate recognition) and Parkhaus Pfaff Areal, Lina-Pfaff-Straße 4a, with 361 spaces (first 15 minutes free, 2.00 euro up to 60 minutes, 4.00 euro up to 120 minutes, 9.00 euro daily maximum).

Q-Park's own pages (read 21 October 2026) show the Pfalztheater garage (Martin-Luther-Straße) with 296 spaces and 10 charging points, open 24/7, and the Stiftsplatz garage with 180 spaces and 3 charging points; no tariffs are shown online for these garages.

APCOA's own page lists the K in Lautern garage (Fackelrondell 1) with 490 spaces, open Monday to Saturday 7:00-22:00 and closed on Sundays, at 1.30 euro for the first hour, 1.50 euro for the second, 2.00 euro per further hour and 23.00 euro daily maximum (read on 21 October 2026). The city's own car-park page for K in Lautern still refers to q-park.de for fees, while Q-Park's current Kaiserslautern page lists only the Pfalztheater and Stiftsplatz garages, so the current operator is not clear from these sources.

The council adopted the Mobilitätsplan Klima+ 2030 on 5 February 2018 (per the city's mobility-plan page). Its report was based on a parking survey in the core zone on Tuesday 8 and Saturday 12 November 2016. It counted about 2,600 spaces in 12 city-centre car parks (about 1,000 of them attributable to long-term parkers) plus about 2,590 on-street spaces, and found car-park occupancy partly below 20 percent and rarely above 70 percent while street parking was often overloaded, especially on Saturday and in the evening. K in Lautern and the Meuthstraße lots were exceptions with very high use; the report called this an indication that the price structure is behind the uneven use (Meuthstraße charged the same as the street, K in Lautern less, at 0.80 euro per hour). Street parking then cost 0.60 to 1.20 euro per hour against 1.50 to 1.80 euro in most garages. The plan proposed making street parking dearer relative to garages and introducing parking management at the university; it does not show which measures were implemented.
items.source_title: Mobilitätsplan Klima+ 2030, Bericht (Stadt Kaiserslautern, February 2018; file dated Aug 2018)

items.text: The city's mobility-data page (undated, read on 21 October 2026) reports the 2023 'Mobilität in Städten' survey (about 1,000 residents): 50 percent of trips were made by car and 50 percent by bus and rail, bicycle and foot, with car use down 3.5 percentage points from the 2018 survey; 19 percent of households have no car, 5.6 percent of cars are electric, and about two thirds of cars are parked on private spaces and one third on public streets.

According to the city's P+R page (undated, read on 21 October 2026), SWK runs free P+R shuttle buses for home matches at the Fritz-Walter-Stadion from P+R KL-Ost (Schweinsdell) and P+R Universität, starting 2.5 hours before kick-off at 5-10 minute intervals, with return trips until about 1.5 hours after the match. The page says there is no public parking in the Betzenberg residential area around the stadium (residents with permits only) and that the match ticket also serves as a VRN public-transport ticket. The page also contains older text referring to the 2010/2011 season, so its currency is uncertain.

A city page on the 'Neue Stadtmitte' realisation (undated, read on 21 October 2026) says the arrival of the K in Lautern shopping centre set off a new inner-city traffic concept and a redesign of its surroundings. The Fruchthallstraße/Fackelbrunnen works (six bus stops grouped, a mobility station with bike and e-scooter hire and e-bike charging) started in September 2022 and were essentially finished in autumn 2023; the page expected the Burgstraße section to follow from 2024, and its current status is not stated.

Under the 2023 fee ordinance, vehicles with an E licence plate may park free at on-street charging posts while charging, for a maximum of 3 hours and with a parking disc displayed. The ordinance does not give the number of public charging points; Q-Park shows 10 points at Pfalztheater and 3 at Stiftsplatz.
items.source_title: Parkgebührenordnung der Stadt Kaiserslautern (in Kraft ab 01.05.2023)

gaps: Current number and operator of public charging points in the centre (SWK e-mobility pages https://www.swk-kl.de/e-mobilitaet read but give no counts; Bundesnetzagentur register not checked).

Tariffs of the Kreissparkasse underground garage (Am Altenhof), Parkhaus Central (Rosenstraße, 70 spaces per directory listings only) and Meuthstraße I/II surface lots: the city page only gives owner contacts or an unexplained note for Meuthstraße II ('Mo-Fr 16:00-24:00, Sa/So ganztags'); the 14% occupancy of Central cannot be explained from official sources.
Q-Park Pfalztheater and Stiftsplatz tariffs are not shown online; opening/closing hours of Altstadt and Pfaff Areal on the Hüfner pages were not fully read.

Capacities in operator pages (City 400, Lutrinastraße 220, Hauptbahnhof 359, Pfalztheater 296, Stiftsplatz 180, Altstadt 372) differ from the figures in our feed; the reason (partly connected spaces, reserved or permit spaces, closed levels) is not documented.

Reason for and reopening date of the May 2025 Hauptbahnhof garage closure: Rheinpfalz articles (https://www.rheinpfalz.de/lokal/kaiserslautern_artikel,-db-parkhaus-gesperrt-das-sind-die-alternativen-_arid,5774475.html and the second one cited) are paywalled beyond the teaser.

The parking fee ordinance of 1 May 2022 (replaced in 2023) and the 2022 council decision on fees were not found; a Rheinpfalz piece of 6 February 2022 (https://www.rheinpfalz.de/lokal/kaiserslautern_artikel,-hanno-scherer-legt-bei-kritik-an-parkgeb%C3%BChren-nach-_arid,5312530.html) only has a teaser (city centre manager criticised fee rises made without consulting traders).

1. FC Kaiserslautern site (fck.de anreise pages) returned HTTP 503 and was not used; no stadium event parking prices or park-and-ride usage figures found. Web search budget ran out before searches on stadium parking, K in Lautern ownership and the Q-Park/APCOA operator change could be done.

No source found for the Verkehrsentwicklungsplan (the mobility plan Klima+ 2030 of 2018 is the closest), a current Innenstadt parking concept, City-Quartier/ECE/Mainzer Tor projects, the university (RPTU Kaiserslautern) parking regime, or US military related parking.

Search-tool summaries wrongly attributed council paper 2025/0171 (parking fee proposal with Salinarium/Wurstmarktplatz) to Kaiserslautern; it concerns another Rhineland-Palatinate town and was not used.
